note: The original uses a comma as the decimal separator, converted here to a point. The alate is unknown. The author notes that the species is small and that, because its habitat is similar to that of P. mwekerae, its identity as a dwarf, juvenile-colony individual of the latter cannot be excluded, so more sampling is needed. Type locality: 40 km along the road from Kasongo-Lunda to Panzi, Congo.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Related to P. minutus but distinctly smaller; compared with P. prorepens the head capsule is not more rectangular and the mandibles are not stouter. Soldier measurements (holotype) head length 1.06 mm, head width 0.85 mm, clearly smaller than in every other species of the genus. The specimens were taken feeding on dead wood in Brachystegia woodland; the nesting habit is unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head capsule yellow; mandibles red, the basal third yellow; postmentum concolorous with the ventral genae. Thoracic and abdominal tergites slightly paler than the head, the anterolateral margins of the pronotum with two dark spots; legs pale yellow. Head capsule nearly rectangular in dorsal view, the sides rounded and slightly converging towards the anterior end; in lateral view the upper and lower surfaces evenly convex, the mentum projecting and its convexity parallel to the ventral genae. Mandibles curved upward, the curvature of the outer margin in dorsal view very similar to that of P. mwekerae; the first marginal tooth of the left mandible very small, the second triangular, with no evident serrations on the inner margin between the second tooth and the base. Postmentum in dorsal view appearing convex on both sides (because the sclerite is inflated), but in fact only very slightly narrowed towards the anterior end. Antenna 14 segments, segment 1 the longest, segment 2 shorter than segment 1, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 (in one individual segment 3 is as long as segment 2 and shows signs of division), segment 4 the shortest, segment 5 as long as wide, segments 6—14 gradually larger. Fontanelle slit-like, indistinct (almost invisible also in P. mwekerae). Head capsule with very sparse hairs; labrum projecting slightly beyond half the length of the mandibles, broadly rounded at the tip, with several long setae.

Soldier measurements (holotype; range for 3 individuals; mm): head length (to the outer mandibular base) 1.06/1.05—1.08; maximum head width 0.85/0.85—0.86; head depth (including the postmentum) 0.67/0.65—0.67; postmentum length 0.73/0.66—0.73; maximum postmentum width 0.37/0.37—0.38; left mandible length 0.57/0.53—0.57; hind tibia length 0.76; maximum pronotum length 0.42/0.40—0.42; pronotum width 0.64/0.63—0.64; mesonotum width 0.58/0.54—0.58; metanotum width 0.68/0.65—0.68.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Large worker: head capsule yellow, with an orange spot on each lateral margin of the postclypeus, hairs sparse; broadly U-shaped in dorsal view, the postclypeus short (its width nearly 3 times its length), its posterior margin straight in the middle, its anterior margin concave, moderately inflated. Labrum long, extending beyond the apex of the closed mandibles. Antenna 16—17 segments. Head width 1.00—1.02 mm.

Small worker: similar to the large worker but paler, the postclypeus more inflated. Head width 0.75 mm.
